\section[recentemente]{recentemente — recently}

\label{lesson:PT-C135-recentemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for which, then the Portuguese for nor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: recentemente}
\textbf{recentemente} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{Recentemente, viajei.} — \textquotedblleft{}Recently I travelled.\textquotedblright{} The ending \textbf{-mente} makes an adverb, the way English uses -ly.

\section[anteontem]{anteontem — the day before yesterday}

\label{lesson:PT-C135-anteontem}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for nor, then the Portuguese for recently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: anteontem}
\textbf{anteontem} — \textquotedblleft{}the day before yesterday\textquotedblright{}. One day further back than yesterday: \textbf{Anteontem escrevi uma mensagem.} — \textquotedblleft{}The day before yesterday I wrote a message.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{escrevi} is the one-word past, like \textbf{falei}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{anteontem}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{anteontem}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for nor, then the Portuguese for recently, then say \emph{anteontem} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does anteontem mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The day before yesterday\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[antigamente]{antigamente — formerly, in the old days}

\label{lesson:PT-C135-antigamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for recently, then the Portuguese for the day before yesterday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: antigamente}
\textbf{antigamente} — \textquotedblleft{}formerly, in the old days\textquotedblright{}. It points to a long stretch of the past, not to one day: \textbf{Antigamente, a loja era aqui.} — \textquotedblleft{}In the old days the shop was here.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{era} is the past of \textbf{ser} for how things used to be.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antigamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{antigamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for recently, then the Portuguese for the day before yesterday, then say \emph{antigamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does antigamente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Formerly, in the old days\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o passado]{o passado — the past}

\label{lesson:PT-C135-o-passado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the day before yesterday, then the Portuguese for formerly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o passado}
\textbf{o passado} — \textquotedblleft{}the past\textquotedblright{}. The same word describes time gone by: \textbf{a semana passada} — \textquotedblleft{}last week\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{o mês passado} — \textquotedblleft{}last month\textquotedblright{}.

\section[acontecer]{acontecer — to happen}

\label{lesson:PT-C135-acontecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for formerly, then the Portuguese for the past.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: acontecer}
\textbf{acontecer} — \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{O que aconteceu?} — \textquotedblleft{}What happened?\textquotedblright{} Like \textbf{falar}, its past is one word: \textbf{falou}, \textbf{aconteceu}.
